An emergency situation suddenly occurs, and the two vehicles brake at the same time. At the beginning of braking, the two vehicles are 30m apart. During braking, the v-t graph of the two vehicles is as shown in the figure. Then which of the following judgments is correct
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The two vehicles will have a rear-end collision after the passenger car stops

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A truck and a passenger car are traveling in the same lane on a highway, with the passenger car in front and the truck behind. An emergency situation suddenly occurs, and the two vehicles brake at the same time. At the beginning of braking, the two vehicles are 30m apart. During braking, the v-t graph of the two vehicles is as shown in the figure. Judge according to the graph: will the two vehicles have a rear-end collision? If so, does the rear-end collision occur before or after the passenger car stops?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The two vehicles will have a rear-end collision after the passenger car stops
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Graph reading: in the figure, the vertical axis is velocity v/(m·s^-1), and the horizontal axis is time t/s. The passenger car velocity straight line descends from (0,40) to (20,0); the truck velocity straight line descends from (0,30) to (30,0); the two straight lines intersect at t=10 s, and the intersection velocity is about 20 m/s. The text of the question gives that the passenger car is in front and the truck is behind, the two vehicles are 30 m apart at the beginning of braking, and they brake at the same time. Reasoning: the area under a v-t graph represents displacement. From 0 to 10 s, the passenger car's speed is greater than the truck's, and the displacement by which the front car travels more than the rear car is the triangular area between the two lines, namely (1/2)×10×10=50 m, so the distance increases from 30 m to 80 m. From 10 to 20 s, the truck's speed is greater than the passenger car's, and the displacement difference recovered by the truck is also the triangular area (1/2)×10×10=50 m, so when the passenger car stops at 20 s, the distance returns to 30 m, and there is not yet a rear-end collision. From 20 to 30 s, the passenger car has stopped, while the truck still continues forward; its remaining displacement is the triangular area (1/2)×10×10=50 m, greater than the remaining 30 m distance at 20 s, so the truck will catch up with the passenger car. Conclusion: the rear-end collision occurs after the passenger car stops.
